name: Ballycarn
questions: Can you send the folio map? The listing says c. 1 acre, but the plot looks like a strip about 25 m wide running about 135 m back from the R148 (nearer 0.8 acre). Does it include the field behind the sheds, and who owns the conifer and the yard to the west?

What is next door: the gravel yard with slabs and a trailer to the west, and the yard with a green-roofed shed and stored materials about 100 m east? Are either of them a business with planning, and what hours do they work?
Is the house on mains water and a septic tank? How old is the tank, and when was the house last wired and plumbed? What heats the radiators: the range in the kitchen, or an oil or gas boiler?

Can you confirm the vacancy dates (empty since when, and whether it's a probate sale) so we can apply for the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant, and can you share the BER cert with its kWh/m²/yr figure (Daft says D1)?
Is there any footpath between the gate and the Johnstown roundabout, and has the site or the road outside ever flooded?

ai.why: €299k plus a rough €110–190k renovation (less grants) is about €350–445k, for a single-storey cottage on about an acre a walk from Enfield's Dublin trains. But at 91 m² it would still need an extension to suit six, it sits on the 80 km/h R148 between yards, and a children's ED is 40–50 minutes away.

electricity.detail: Likely connected or easily reconnected: a pole and line run to the house, and the photos show radiators and sockets; vacant over two years, so check the supply and the wiring.

water.detail: Not stated. The ribbon of houses on the R148 may be on public mains; a private well is the alternative. Ask.

sewer.detail: Not stated; a septic tank is likely 1.5 km outside the town. Ask its age and condition, and budget for an upgrade.

internet.detail: Not confirmed: the listing doesn't mention broadband and BuyerIQ shows 'no data'. Siro and open eir fibre cover Enfield town 1–1.5 km away, and a pole runs to the house; check the Eircode with ComReg/NBI.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: Single-storey cottage (the floor plan has one floor and the photos show no upper windows), so all four bedrooms are on the ground floor. The best one for Gabor's parents is the 4.56 × 4.11 m front bedroom off the rear hall, nearest the bathroom and WC.

bedsNote: Four bedrooms on one level: 4.56 × 4.11 m, 3.41 × 2.87 m, and two small rooms of 2.13 × 3.02 m and 2.26 × 3.02 m. There's one bathroom (3.44 × 2.92 m) and a separate WC (2.14 × 1.17 m). The living room is 4.49 × 3.14 m, the kitchen 3.44 × 2.98 m. Outbuildings: a green steel shed, a second shed and a derelict timber shed.
heating: Not stated; the photos show radiators, a solid-fuel range in the kitchen and a stove in the living room
tagline: A vacant single-storey 4-bed cottage of about 91 m² needing complete modernisation, on a long strip of about an acre on the R148, 1.5 km east of Enfield and its Dublin train.

pros.detail: Stamp duty about €2,990 (Daft's figure). Even with a rough €110–190k renovation, less €50–70k of grants, it lands around €350–445k all-in.

pros.text: Every bedroom on the ground floor
pros.detail: The floor plan has one level and no stairs. The 4.56 × 4.11 m front bedroom suits Gabor's parents, a few steps from the bathroom and WC.

Enfield station is 1.5 km in a straight line, 1.8 km and about 24 minutes on foot (OSM routing), or 3 minutes by car. Ten Dublin-bound trains each weekday (06:32–21:17); the eight Sligo intercity services reach Connolly in 47–65 minutes.

pros.text: About an acre for the dogs
pros.detail: The listing says c. 1 acre. From above it's a long strip about 25 m wide running about 135 m back from the road to a hedge, roughly 0.8 acre by the satellite estimate, with fields behind.

pros.text: Town and schools a short hop
pros.detail: SuperValu is about 1 km away in a straight line and Enfield Community College 1.1 km. St Mary's Primary (570 pupils, mixed) is in the town, so school runs are minutes.

pros.text: Grants should cover a slice of the work
pros.detail: The listing says it has been vacant 'well in excess of two years', which meets the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant test (up to €50k, more if derelict); SEAI energy grants stack on top.
A renovated 4-bed with land, a walk from a commuter station on the M4 corridor, should rent readily when the family is away.

cons.detail: Rough: shower room or en suite from the WC and a hall cupboard €12–20k (€35–50k as an extension); D1 to B2 with wall and attic insulation, windows and a heat pump €45–75k before €15–25k of SEAI grants; kitchen €15–25k; rewiring and replumbing €18–30k; finishes €15–30k; a septic upgrade €8–15k if needed. The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant (up to €50k) could offset much of it.

The floor-plan rooms add up to 91 m², under the brief's 100 m². The living room is 4.49 × 3.14 m and the kitchen 3.44 × 2.98 m, too small for six, and two bedrooms are about 6.5 m². Making it work probably means an extension (rough €2,500–3,000/m²).

cons.text: One bathroom and a WC for six
cons.detail: One 3.44 × 2.92 m bathroom plus a 2.14 × 1.17 m WC; a second shower room is a must.

cons.text: On the R148 at 80 km/h, no footpath at the gate
cons.detail: The house sits about 20 m from the old N4 (R148, 80 km/h, unlit), and OSM maps no footpath on the 300 m to the Johnstown roundabout. The walk to town starts on the hard shoulder, and the front needs fencing for the dogs.

cons.text: Yards and houses close on both sides
cons.detail: From above: houses about 25–35 m away on each side, in a ribbon of about ten along the road. The lot to the west is a gravel yard with slabs and a trailer, there's a yard with a green-roofed shed and stockpiled materials about 100 m east, and a cluster of sheds with wrapped bales about 140 m to the north-east across the road.

BuyerIQ lists a 65-unit scheme being built on the lands north of the Johnstown roundabout, and 8 large residential applications about 250 m away. Expect years of construction traffic, with Enfield spreading towards the house.
Naas and Connolly take 16+ only; Regional Hospital Mullingar (about 50 km) and CHI Temple Street or Tallaght in Dublin (about 40–45 km) take children.
Water, sewer, heating and broadband aren't stated; BuyerIQ shows 2 hidden critical and 4 high-priority flags behind its paid report (and mislabels the house as a 2-bed new home).
